title: Traffic Stop: Search & Questions
description: You are pulled over at night.

choices.feedback: You gave consent.

choices.text: I do not consent to searches
choices.feedback: Correct.
You may incriminate yourself.
Talking can hurt you.
Correct.

title: Police at Your Door
description: Two officers knock on your front door. They say they want to ask a few questions.

start.question: Officer: 'Mind if we come in and look around?'

choices.feedback: Letting them in is consent — anything in view can now be used.
Correct. Without a warrant, you don't have to open the door.

let_in.question: Inside, an officer starts asking about your roommate.

choices.feedback: Your statements can be used against you or others.

choices.text: I'd like you to leave now
choices.feedback: You can revoke consent at any time.

warrant_question.question: Officer: 'We don't need a warrant to talk. Just open up.'

choices.feedback: Opening the door can become implied consent to enter.

choices.text: Speak through the door: 'I don't consent to entry.'
choices.feedback: Correct. You may speak through the door and refuse entry without a warrant.

end_good.result: You protected your home — no warrant, no entry.

end_ok.result: You recovered by revoking consent, but letting them in exposed you.

end_bad.result: You gave up your strongest protection: the home.

title: Stopped on the Street
description: An officer approaches you on the sidewalk and starts asking questions.

start.question: Officer: 'Where are you headed? Got any ID on you?'

choices.text: Hand over ID and explain your whole day
choices.feedback: In many states you aren't required to show ID unless detained or driving.

choices.text: Am I being detained, or am I free to go?
choices.feedback: Correct. This forces the officer to clarify the stop's legal status.

talking.question: Officer keeps asking questions about a nearby incident.

choices.feedback: Innocent explanations can still be used against you.
You can invoke your right to silence at any point.

choices.text: Repeat calmly: 'Am I free to go?'
choices.feedback: Correct. If you're not detained, you may walk away calmly.

choices.text: Walk away without a word, quickly
choices.feedback: Sudden flight can create suspicion; clarify first, then leave calmly.

end_good.result: You clarified the stop and protected your rights.

end_ok.result: You stopped the bleeding by going silent, but shared more than needed.

end_bad.result: You volunteered information you never had to give.

title: Filming at a Protest
description: You are recording police at a public demonstration. An officer approaches you.

start.question: Officer: 'Turn that camera off and hand me the phone.'

choices.feedback: You are generally not required to surrender your phone on demand.

choices.text: Keep filming from a distance: 'I have a right to record.'
choices.feedback: Correct. Recording police in public is broadly protected — as long as you don't interfere.

phone_taken.question: Officer: 'Unlock it so I can delete the video.'

choices.feedback: Deleting your footage may destroy evidence; you don't have to unlock anything.

choices.text: 'I do not consent to a search of my phone.'
choices.feedback: Correct. Phone searches generally require a warrant.

keeps_filming.question: Officer: 'You're interfering with an arrest. Step back.'

choices.feedback: Physical interference can turn protected recording into an arrestable act.
Correct. Comply with distance orders while continuing to record.

end_good.result: You kept your footage and your rights.

end_ok.result: You protected your phone's contents, but surrendering it weakened your position.

end_bad.result: You gave up evidence and protections you were entitled to keep.

title: Passenger in a Traffic Stop
description: The car you're riding in gets pulled over. The officer looks at you.

start.question: Officer: 'You too — let me see some ID.'

choices.feedback: Volunteering information helps no one in the car.

choices.text: 'Am I being detained, or am I free to go?'
choices.feedback: Correct. Passengers can ask whether they are free to leave; ID rules for passengers vary by state.

talking.question: Officer: 'So whose stuff is in the back seat?'

choices.text: Speculate about what's in the car
choices.feedback: Guessing about others' property can implicate you or them.
You can stop answering at any point.

detained_question.question: Officer: 'Just sit tight.' The driver is asked to step out.

choices.text: Get out and walk off without asking
choices.feedback: Leaving mid-stop without clarifying can escalate the situation.

choices.text: Stay calm, stay put, say nothing further
choices.feedback: Correct. Stay composed and let the stop conclude.

end_good.result: You stayed calm and gave up nothing.

end_ok.result: You recovered by going silent after saying too much.

end_bad.result: You volunteered information or escalated a routine stop.

title: Phone Search Request
description: After a brief stop, an officer asks about your phone.

start.question: Officer: 'Mind unlocking your phone so I can take a quick look?'

choices.feedback: Consent opens everything on the device to inspection.

choices.text: 'I do not consent to a search of my phone.'
choices.feedback: Correct. Searching a phone generally requires a warrant, even after an arrest.

unlocked.question: Officer scrolls through your messages and asks about a text.

choices.feedback: Explanations of private messages can be used against you or others.

choices.text: 'I'm revoking consent. Please return my phone.'
choices.feedback: You can withdraw consent, though what was seen has been seen.

refused.question: Officer: 'If you have nothing to hide, why not?'

choices.feedback: Pressure doesn't create a legal obligation — this is still consent.

choices.text: Stay polite and firm: 'I don't consent to searches.'
choices.feedback: Correct. Repeating a calm refusal preserves your rights.

end_good.result: Your phone and its contents stayed private.

end_ok.result: You cut the search short, but consent already exposed some of it.

end_bad.result: You consented away the strongest privacy protection you had.
